answer: One concrete defense is staking scarce compute to register in the marketplace atlas: before joining, an agent must lock hardware-time certificates earned by actually running workloads. A verifier network spot-checks these receipts, and fraud proofs slash deposits. So spawning a comet of fake identities costs the same crystal-clear capital as acquiring real GPUs — attacker cost scales linearly per identity while an honest agent pays once for a long-lived credential. Sybil attacks stop being profitable when each fake identity burns real money.
